title: Attacks on Indians Abroad Surged From 29 to Over 100 a Year in Five Years, MEA Data Shows
excerpt: Ministry of External Affairs data tabled in Parliament reveals the US recorded the highest number of attacks on Indian nationals from 2021 to 2025, with Ireland and the UK emerging as new hotspots.
body:
• Attacks on Indians abroad rose from 29 in 2021 to 109 in 2023, before declining to 107 in 2024 and 50 in 2025 (through mid-year), per MEA data tabled in Parliament
  • The United States recorded the highest cumulative attacks over 2022-2025, with 10, 12, 9, and 3 incidents respectively
  • 91 attacks on Indian students were recorded over five years, resulting in 30 deaths — Canada topped the list with 27 attacks and 16 fatalities
  • Ireland has emerged as a new concern, with the Indian embassy issuing safety advisories after a surge in racially motivated assaults in 2025

The number of reported attacks on Indian nationals abroad has surged dramatically over the past five years, rising from 29 incidents in 2021 to a peak of 109 in 2023, according to Ministry of External Affairs data tabled in a Rajya Sabha response in August 2025.

The figures, covering 45 countries, show attacks climbed from 29 in 2021 to 52 in 2022, then more than doubled to 109 in 2023. The count remained elevated at 107 in 2024 before declining to 50 in the first half of 2025 — though the full-year figure is expected to be higher.

US Leads in Total Attacks

The United States recorded the highest number of attacks over the four-year period from 2022 to 2025, with 10 incidents in 2022, 12 in 2023, nine in 2024, and three in the first half of 2025. Sri Lanka reported the second-highest totals, driven by attacks on Indian fishermen, with 14 in 2022 and 30 in 2023.

Canada, home to one of the largest Indian diaspora populations, saw six attacks in 2022, 10 in 2023, nine in 2024, and three in early 2025. The United Kingdom recorded two attacks in 2022 that spiked to 10 in 2023 before falling back to five in 2024.

Other notable patterns emerged in Russia, which went from zero recorded attacks in 2022 to 12 in 2023, and Germany, which saw 12 incidents in 2024 alone after recording none in the two preceding years.

Indian Students Bear a Disproportionate Burden

Separate MEA data reveals that 91 attacks on Indian students were recorded over five years, resulting in 30 deaths. Canada accounted for the largest share with 27 student attacks and 16 fatalities. Russia saw 15 incidents but no deaths, while the UK recorded 12 attacks with one death.

"There has been an increase in the instances of physical attacks against Indian citizens in Ireland recently. The Embassy is in touch with authorities concerned."

— Indian Embassy in Dublin, advisory issued August 2025

The United States recorded nine attacks on students — all fatal — making it the deadliest country per incident for Indian students abroad. Germany reported 11 attacks with one death, and Australia four with one fatality.

Ireland Emerges as a New Flashpoint

Ireland has become one of the most concerning new hotspots. In July 2025, a recently arrived Indian tech worker was brutally attacked, robbed, and stripped in Tallaght, Dublin, after a group of teenagers falsely accused him of inappropriate behavior — baseless claims that had been amplified by far-right social media accounts. In a separate incident the same month, an Indian student suffered a broken nose and severe bruises in an unprovoked racial attack in the same area.

The Indian embassy in Dublin issued a formal advisory urging citizens to "take reasonable precautions for their personal security and avoid deserted areas, especially during odd hours." An Indian-origin entrepreneur, Dr. Santosh Yadav, described being beaten by six teenagers near his apartment, suffering a fractured cheekbone.

Why Attacks Are Rising

Analysts point to a confluence of factors: rising xenophobia fueled by far-right movements, housing and labor market competition in host countries, and online misinformation that frames Indian immigrants as symbols of unchecked migration. A 2025 Pew Research study across 24 countries found that while 47% held a favorable view of India, unfavorable perceptions often translate into prejudice against diaspora communities.

An RTI response by activist Dr. Vivek Pandey revealed that 28,458 Indians died abroad over three years, including 136 due to violence or murder.

What the Diaspora Should Know

The Indian government has issued country-specific advisories and lodged diplomatic protests following individual incidents, but has not released a consolidated global strategy addressing diaspora safety. Experts say stronger diplomatic engagement, improved emergency response networks, and coordinated monitoring with host nations are needed to protect the growing Indian population abroad, estimated at over 32 million including students, workers, and permanent residents.
